title: Rabbi Elazar of Hagronia
author: Aharon Hyman

paragraphs: He was Rava’s student, as in Taanit 24b: Rava decreed a fast and rain did not come. He said to them: “Is there anyone who saw a dream? Let him tell it.” Rabbi Elazar of Hagronia said to him: “In my dream they read to me: ‘Good greetings to a good master from a good Lord, who from His goodness does good to His people.’” He said: “Learn from this that it is a time of favor.” In Eruvin 63a it is related that Rabbi Elazar of Hagronia and Rav Acha bar Tachlifa visited Rav Acha son of Rav Ika in the place of Rav Acha bar Yaakov. Rav Acha son of Rav Ika brought them a knife to examine; Rav Acha bar Tachlifa did not want to examine it out of respect for Rav Acha bar Yaakov, who was the eldest among them, but Rabbi Elazar of Hagronia said to him, “Thus said Rava: A Torah scholar may examine for himself,” and he was punished for this. Bava Metzia 69a relates that Rabbi Elazar of Hagronia bought an animal and gave it to a sharecropper for half the profit. In the end, when they divided, he gave the sharecropper, besides half the profit, also the head. The sharecropper’s wife said to her husband: “If you joined him as a partner, he would give you the tail as well.” He did so, and in the end the sharecropper lost even half of the head, for Rabbi Elazar said to him, “Now we are partners,” etc.

notes.text: Elazar follows the full headword. The employee joins Elazar as a partner in the revised arrangement; the wife’s proposed improvement instead loses him half of the formerly separate head payment. The source’s abridged dialogue and punishment account remain as supplied.

The consulted Eruvin 63a first calls the visitor Abba bar Tachlifa and then Acha bar Tachlifa; Hyman supplies Acha. The text explicitly attributes the examination and punishment to Elazar of Hagronia. Bava Metzia 69a directly preserves the employee’s move into partnership and loss of the formerly separate head payment; Hyman’s abbreviated quoted ending is retained as supplied.
